Standard practice: Operate at 200°C to maximize reaction rate and equilibrium conversion, accepting a steady-state DMT concentration in the liquid phase that exceeds the solubility/precipitation threshold at the cooler wall, causing esterification-wall fouling.
My mitigation: Lower the temperature setpoint from 200°C to 185°C. This is a genuine departure because it intentionally trades reaction rate for a significant drop in the steady-state DMT concentration. While the absolute reaction rate drops, the equilibrium conversion of methanol to ester increases at the lower temperature (due to the exothermic nature of the esterification and the dilution effect of the methanol excess), fundamentally changing the chemical composition of the bulk liquid to one that is less prone to wall-phase separation.
